thesis: Explicit reasoning circuits become useful when their interfaces preserve relevant semantic distinctions, but explicitness alone establishes neither discovery efficiency nor worldly truth.
role: Chapters 1–4 establish operational understanding, circuit objects and compositional contracts.

ideas.statement: Histories may share continuation only when relevant future observations cannot distinguish them.
Domain-relative understanding includes coherent answers, missing-information diagnosis and revision under changed premises.
Source statements, interpretations, world claims and kinds of uncertainty must remain distinguishable.
Circuit source, executed instance and materialized content are distinct; SSA names do not remove loops or effects.
Semantic contracts support composition, but compatibility does not select a useful construction or supply missing context.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Warehouse quantities require temporal and availability interpretations before arithmetic; conditional answers may be appropriate.
Lending and permanent transfer can agree on possession while differing in ownership.
An entire retained execution can be too expensive or unusable for human audit.
SOP Lang proposes a common circuit form for knowledge, rules, interpretation and composition strategies.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Methodological circuit models do not imply that reality itself is a circuit or solve consciousness.
DisCoCirc is an acknowledged precedent, not an invention claimed here.
Accepted circuits hide rejected search paths; both discovery and result costs matter.

audit.notes: Read every unit; preserve proposed versus demonstrated status.
